title: Rivers: water from the network
brief:
GOAL
Small streams are drawn by the drainage network itself: every wet channel carries water unbroken from its head to the river or sea it joins, always downhill, never perched above its banks or on a ridge, smooth through its bends and joins.

WHY
Phase 1 (job rivers-probe, bun check:streams) showed the network is plausible but mostly undrawn: 46-99% of wet path samples have no water. Water is assigned to whichever channel owns the lowest land, so a coarser or same-level valley steals it (55% + 12% of breaks) and in ranges water perches over a lower neighbouring valley (61% of samples >0.5 block, p95 34). World gates drop more: BANK next to grid rivers (23-29% on the default world) and low ground (terrain <= 1, 77% of the 100k plain's level 1). Bend noise folds (fold-area 6-25% on levels 2-6), and ~1/4 of joins meet their parent at >90 degrees, against its flow. Decision with the human: the network is the truth, land and water obey it.

CONTEXT
- Repo /home/cody/git/terraverse; follow its AGENTS.md (fixed point, terragen pure, a generation change bumps the generator version and a golden pins it; run bun check:terragen after).
- apps/game/src/terragen/channels.{h,cpp}: Channels::read() (bend ~L1160-1190, lowest-land ownership + water ~L1268-1288, STREAM_SINKS ~L1378, then rolls/beds/step/keep reshaping land).
- World gates you found (BANK, low-ground) in World's ground() path, apps/game/src/terragen/world.cpp.
- Your probe: scripts/stream-check/ (bun check:streams); keep its constants in sync if you change them in channels.cpp.

APPROACH
1. Water from the network: a wet segment (flow >= STREAM_FLOW) draws its water along its whole line regardless of which channel owns the lowest land; its level interpolates bed low..high along the line. Where several wet segments are near, take the nearest line (larger flow wins ties).
2. Land obeys water: within a wet channel's floor/banks, clamp land so it never stands above that channel's bed + a small bank, and make the post-water reshaping (rolls, benches/step, keep, fans, sills) yield there. Retire STREAM_SINKS for drawn streams.
3. Bends never fold: bound the bend so its slope stays < 1 (amplitude vs wavelength), or equivalent; joins meet the parent going downstream (no angle > 90 degrees against its flow).
4. World gates: a stream reaching a grid river's bank or the sea/low ground continues to it rather than being dropped.
Keep the land's overall shape (valleys/ridges from hillsides) as is: this is about where water goes and the land right under it.

CONSTRAINTS
- Only terragen (channels.*, world.* as needed) plus the probe and goldens/version. No far/, planetarium, or mapgen changes beyond what a version bump requires.
- Determinism and generation speed: report column-time before/after (scripts/terragen-check perf tool or equivalent); no more than ~10% slower without saying so.
- Don't commit. Check git status before editing; if anyone else has uncommitted changes in files you need, stop and report blocked.

OUT OF SCOPE
Grid-scale rivers (they look good), fans/karst sinking as features (later, deliberately), map rendering (sprint 114).

DONE WHEN
- bun check:streams: break% < 2% on every region (unfound excluded), joins >90 degrees against flow = 0, fold-area 0, perched-over-bank p95 < 1 block, uphill 0.
- bun check:terragen passes with the version bumped and goldens updated.
- Before/after PNGs for each region, and the same example coordinates from phase 1 shown fixed.
- Two runs identical.

REPORT
STATUS / CHANGED / DECISIONS / EVIDENCE / QUESTIONS.

text: Captain: this job is now the rivers thread log (phase 1 is rivers-probe, verified). Phase 2 is in progress per the brief. Worker: from now on append notes and your report here as rivers-commander.

Progress: water now drawn from the network (nearest wet line), land clamped to it after toGrid/beds (banks up, channel cut), STREAM_SINKS retired; bends BEND_SHARE 12 / BEND_WAVES 2 (fold-area 0); joins slid 60deg downstream, never squarer than 75 or past a foot (conf>90 = 0); same-level crossings rejected in build(); World BANK/low gates lifted for prototype land; water kept to grid via per-node inherited grid/over heights. Probe: break% <2 all regions, fold 0, conf>90 0. Remaining: uphill 16 samples (r100k-belt, crossing-like water jumps), perched p95, then version bump/goldens/perf.

Finding: with water from the network, ~42% (r100k-belt) / 21% (r100k-plain) of drawn stream samples sit on a dyke: the network bed stands tens of blocks over a coarser valley's floor the line runs inside (e.g. L3 at 356 over a level-2 trough floor at 317.5). Banks (land raised to water+1) hide it from the perched metric; probe now has a far-out ridge test that shows it. Tried: inherited keep (no effect), beds on water (none), flat run across the parent's floor (none), rejecting crossings of level-above lines (no effect on dykes, breaks up). Needs a design call. Also: uphill/crossing fixed via shared bend fade (Read::bent); probe artefacts fixed (sea, inverse warp, perched-in-water).

STATUS     partial: blocked on a design call. Breaks, folds, joins and uphill are fixed. But drawing water from the network shows its beds often stand far above the land round them, and the current answer (raising banks) leaves streams on dykes. No version bump or golden update was done. The TestTerragen unit run was still going when I stopped.

CHANGED
- apps/game/src/terragen/channels.cpp
  - Water comes from the network: the wet line whose edge is nearest. Each line's level is that segment's bed, brought to the grid by toGrid's map; the grid heights it uses come from the segment's foot (what it joins) and rise toward its head.
  - The land gives way after toGrid/beds. Banks are raised to the water plus 1 block, falling at 0.33 a block past that. The channel is cut down to the water. Both stay within a corridor of 8 blocks or 3 widths.
  - STREAM_SINKS is retired. Fans no longer lift the water.
  - Bends are gentler: BEND_SHARE 12 and BEND_WAVES 2, so they never fold.
  - A level's bend now fades by distance to the level above's lines, the same for all its channels, instead of fading toward each segment's own foot. That per-segment fade made same-level lines cross, so one stream's water stood over another's. Read::bent exposes where each level is measured from.
  - Joins slide downstream to come in at about 60° (JOIN_DOWN 0.58). Joins that would face upstream, come in squarer than 75°, or slide past the target's foot are rejected.
  - In build(), a node's way down that crosses a lower same-level line within 2 cells is rejected.
  - A join to the level above longer than 2.75 lattices on any axis costs FAR_COST more. It is taken only when nothing nearer exists, because read()'s window can't gather it.
  - Shape::flat: a tributary runs level across the floor of what it joins before climbing. This had no measurable effect on dykes.
- apps/game/src/terragen/channels.h: new Shape fields grid_low/high, over_low/high and flat; the same on Segment; Read::bent; overGrid() and rangeAt().
- apps/game/src/terragen/world.cpp: the stream gate in ground() no longer requires terrain > 1 or a gap of BANK from a grid river, on prototype land.
- scripts/stream-check/probe.cpp
  - Bends now come from Read::bent, so no private constants are duplicated.
  - Break means no water drawn on the line, the stream's own or another's.
  - New counts: "sea" (it has reached the sea) and "karst" (a deliberate feature). Neither counts as a break.
  - The inverse warp is damped. Before, it missed the column by about 1 block, which faked w:other and w:low breaks.
  - A bank counts only where no water is drawn on it.
  - "over p50/p95" is now taken over all samples with water.
  - Ridge now also flags a dyke: land 24 blocks or 4 widths out lower than the water minus 1.

DECISIONS
- Phase 1's break definition (the stream's own water) became "any water drawn on its line". Streams side by side and at confluences cover each other. To compare honestly, I re-ran the new probe against HEAD in a temporary worktree.
- Phase 1 counted much of r100k-plain wrongly. Most of that region is sea (91% of samples), which phase 1 called w:low breaks. Those samples are now "sea" and excluded.
- Karst sinking is excluded as out of scope, as your brief says.
- I did not bump the version (TF22 → TF23 touches 32 files, including player-facing codes) or update goldens. The generation isn't settled (the dyke question below), so bumping now would have to be redone.
- Departure from APPROACH: raising banks (step 2 plus a bank rise) was needed to meet the perched target. But it turns "water perched over a lower valley" into "stream on a dyke over the land".

EVIDENCE
- Command: `bun check:streams`, about 25 s. Two runs gave identical text and PNG md5s.

Before is HEAD measured with the same new probe; after is now. These are the "all" rows.

| Region | break% | conf>90 | uphill (worst) | fold-area | over-bank p95 | dyke/ridge% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default-plain | 63.7 → 0.0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0.9 → 0 | — → 0.1 | 0 → 0 |
| default-river | 38.9 → 0.0 | 9 → 0 | 4 (0.4) → 0 | 0.9 → 0 | 0.2 → 0.7 | — → 0.6 |
| r100k-belt | 49.3 → 0.1 | 25 → 0 | 36 (0.7) → 1 (0.4) | 8–22 by level → 0 | 26.1 → 0.0 | — → 42.1 |
| r100k-plain | 85.2 → 2.2 | 133 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 6–25 by level → 0 | 0.0 → 0.3 | — → 20.6 |

- r100k-plain's 2.2% is 0.2% of all samples: a level-2 segment 2051 blocks long, the far fallback, at the coast where nothing nearer exists.
- Perf (columns, perf.cpp, 3 runs): default 3.6–3.9 → 3.6–3.9 µs; 100k 5.2–5.4 → 5.1–5.2 µs. No slower.
- `bun check:terragen` end-to-end: 43/43 columns agree; core.terra, weather and the weather on the world all pass. The TestTerragen unit run had not finished after more than 20 minutes. The golden test will fail, since generation changed and no bump was made.
- Images, before and after:
  - .output/stream-check/before/{default-plain,default-river,r100k-belt,r100k-plain}.png
  - .output/stream-check/after/ (same names), plus report.txt in each folder.
  - In after/r100k-belt.png the dykes show as raised berms across the flat ground.
- Phase 1's example coordinates:
  - default 0.232788,0.225922: 79/81 water. 0.208725,0.261719 (the grid-river BANK gate): 80/81.
  - 100k belt examples now miss: the network itself moved (joins and bends changed), so those points no longer lie on streams.
  - 100k plain 0.995728,0.178558 and 0.999146,0.178772 are open sea: phase 1 got them wrong.
- The dyke cause, measured with banks turned off: water stands up to about 95 blocks (p95) over its banks in r100k-belt. For example, a level-3 bed at 356 stands over a level-2 floor at 317.5, the stream's line lying across or inside that coarser floor near its head.

QUESTIONS
- Decision needed: where a stream's bed stands over a coarser valley's floor it lies across, what should give?
  - (a) Keep dykes: the current state, which fails "never on a ridge".
  - (b) Lower the water to the land: the stream sits in the land, but it can run uphill or break where the land dips.
  - (c) Change the network so such channels join that coarser valley, or don't exist. That means a cost or check in build()/toLevelAbove against coarser floors, not just lines.
  - My recommendation is (c): make a node's bed never exceed any coarser channel's ground along its line when choosing its join. This needs the coarser floors' widths in the join cost, a deeper rework of the join choice.
- Version bump: once the design is settled, bump TF22 → TF23 across all 32 files, or bump the golden alone, as the recent commits did?
